answer: Make each identity grow its own timber chain: a memory-hard sequential proof, so clones cannot share one chain and one machine cannot run n chains in parallel. A violet beacon summons random identities to recompute; copied work fails because its memory trace cannot be replayed. Influence scales with the square root of bonded stake, and identities caught sharing work suffer joint slashing. A hollow shell with no chain earns nothing. Splitting into n identities multiplies sequential cost by n, while joint-slash loss grows with n squared, so forgery costs rise faster than the identities bought.
